title: Hypoglycaemia at a charity event
setting: Charity event. 40M behaving oddly, grumpy, argumentative, unsteady on feet, pale, sweaty. Known Type 1 diabetic.
verdictExplanation: Diabetic patient with blood glucose of 3.2 mmol/L, altered mental status (grumpy, confused), and autonomic symptoms (sweaty, pale). Sick: needs immediate glucose treatment.

shared.response: Responding but very confused and argumentative
shared.circulation: Extremely pale, cold, and clammy skin

history.history: Missed lunch because he was covering a stall, had breakfast early at 6am
history.additional: Friend reports he is normally very friendly, not aggressive

followUp.question: What is the first-line treatment for this patient while he is still able to swallow?

options.text: Give 15-20g of fast-acting sugar (sugary drink, sweets, or gel) and reassess in 15 minutes
Administer his regular dose of insulin to stabilize his blood sugar
Lie him flat on his back, elevate his legs, and give him water
Tell him to rest quietly in a dark room until the event ends

followUp.explanation: Symptomatic low blood sugar requires immediate oral fast-acting sugar. Giving insulin is highly dangerous. Water does not raise blood sugar. Rest without treatment will lead to unconsciousness.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Give sugary food/drink immediately if conscious. If unresponsive, recovery position and 999.
levelFlags.erNotes: Measure BGL. Treat with oral glucose. If unresponsive, administer glucagon IM (if trained) or call 999 and protect airway. Monitor vitals closely.
